# **Research Gap Audit: Dead-Disk Referential Graphs for Stateless Cross-Artifact Inference**

Yes—there is a genuine, publishable research gap behind **Dead-Disk Referential Graphs (Stateless Cross-Artifact Inference)**, and the core idea is substantially stronger than incremental DFIR visualization proposals. However, the gap is **narrower and more specific** than your initial pitch frames it. Individual components of the concept already exist in separate lineages: commercial forensics constructs non-temporal artifact link graphs (Magnet AXIOM Connections)1, recent open-source and academic DFIR frameworks encode cold-disk artifacts into RDF/CASE knowledge graphs for deterministic contradiction or deduction rules (the IoI Framework and FEAR)2, tabular ML pipelines already prioritize post-mortem Windows artifacts without live kernel sensors (reaching 0.96 ROC-AUC across 6,271 compromised systems)4, and USENIX Security 2024 introduced a logless spatial-snapshot provenance graph with weight propagation (ARTISAN)6.  
What remains **genuinely unresearched** across the surveyed security venues (USENIX Security, IEEE S\&P, NDSS, ACM CCS, ASIA CCS, EuroS\&P) and DFIR venues (DFRWS, *Forensic Science International: Digital Investigation*, DFDS) is the exact intersection you are proposing: **reconstructing a typed, pointer-resolved referential graph purely from a single cold post-mortem Windows NTFS image—without runtime kernel telemetry, EVTX logs, prior filesystem snapshots, or timestamp correlation—and executing hub-attenuated anomaly score propagation across those static pointers to surface contextually malicious but individually benign entities (such as Microsoft-signed LOLBins triggered by anomalous persistence chains or DLL sideloading exposed in Prefetch module graphs).**  
Converting this unoccupied intersection into an accepted paper—rather than an immediate Related Work rejection—requires correcting two overstated claims in your framing ("every security graph paper uses runtime telemetry" and "every dead-disk forensic tool treats artifacts as flat timestamped CSVs") and directly solving three technical problems native to cold Windows NTFS graphs: **silent pointer-resolution breakage** (hosting-app Prefetch command-line hashing, MFT sequence-number reuse, multi-hop COM/ServiceDll indirection, and Amcache 31 MiB prefix hashes), **static hub collapse** (universal OS DLLs and polymorphic LOLBin supernodes causing score smearing or over-smoothing), and **post-2025 evaluation rigor** (rule–label leakage, unverified benign baselines, and multi-seed instability).

## **Deconstructing Your Premises Against the 2024–2026 Landscape**

Reviewers will test your novelty claim by dissecting its three underlying assertions: whether security graph papers exclusively require runtime kernel telemetry, whether dead-disk forensic tooling remains purely flat and timeline-bound, and whether static cross-artifact score propagation is truly missing. Mapping representative systems across both communities exposes exactly where prior art stops and where Concept A begins.  
![][image1]

### **Where Premise 1 Holds—and the Three Exceptions Reviewers Will Cite**

Your first premise—that security graph detectors depend on runtime kernel telemetry such as Sysmon, ETW, or Linux Auditd—accurately describes the mainstream Provenance-based Intrusion Detection System (PIDS) literature. A USENIX Security 2025 systematization by Bilot et al. evaluated eight leading PIDS architectures (SIGL, THREATRACE, NODLINK, MAGIC, KAIROS, FLASH, R-CAID, and ORTHRUS) and confirmed that all rely on dynamic system-call streams capturing processes, files, and network flows over DARPA benchmarks7. Likewise, foundational graph score-propagation and root-cause investigation systems—including NoDoze (NDSS 2019), MORSE (IEEE S\&P 2020), DepImpact (USENIX Security 2022), Dossier (NDSS 2022), TAPAS (USENIX Security 2025), and GRAAL (EuroS\&P 2026)—depend on continuous OS auditing frameworks such as Linux Audit, CamFlow, or ETW8. Even recent Windows persistence classifiers like DAPTASK (2025), which achieved a 95.19% F1-score on malicious Scheduled Tasks, depend on Sysmon log streams rather than cold disk artifacts15.  
Claiming that *every* security graph paper uses runtime telemetry, however, invites immediate pushback citing three distinct non-runtime or non-audit graph lineages. The closest security paper you must explicitly differentiate in your introduction is **ARTISAN (USENIX Security 2024\)**6. ARTISAN abandons continuous temporal audit logging on resource-constrained IoT devices in favor of spatial filesystem snapshots (copy-on-write deltas paired with ZFS nounlink preservation)6. It parses ELF binaries, Dalvik apps, and 25 document formats into a Universal File Model (UFM), infers causal links via Datalog rules to construct a Content Provenance Graph (CPG), weights similarity edges using TF-IDF to create a Weighted Content Provenance Graph (WCPG), and applies weight propagation to isolate attack subgraphs—achieving 93.9% average precision and 98.8% recall across 16 IoT attack scenarios compared to ALchemist's 78.4% precision and 95.3% recall, at 3.68% runtime overhead6. Despite its logless framing, ARTISAN does not occupy your gap: it requires proactive pre-attack instrumentation to capture periodic multi-snapshot deltas and preserve unlinked files over time, and it correlates IoT file contents rather than Windows OS persistence and execution artifacts on a single uninstrumented cold NTFS disk6.  
A second exception is **fleet-wide file-relation and DNS propagation graphs**. Symantec's Polonium (Chau et al., 2011\) ran Belief Propagation over an undirected bipartite graph exceeding 37 billion edges across 48 million machines and 903 million files17, while AESOP (KDD 2014\) used Locality-Sensitive Hashing over 119 million machines and 10.1 billion files to propagate reputation across co-occurring files, achieving early detection of 79% of unlabeled malware and 99% of benign files at a 0.0001 false positive rate19. Ni et al. (WISE 2015\) similarly applied label propagation over k-NN file-relation graphs21, and numerous enterprise network detectors propagate scores across host–domain DNS or HTTP graphs24. None of these methods can function on a single cold disk because they depend on cross-host prevalence and fleet co-occurrence, which do not exist during single-endpoint dead-disk triage.  
A third recent exception is **graph-based volatile memory forensics**, exemplified by an October 2026 arXiv preprint (arXiv:2611.01225, Chudasama et al.) that pairs a temperature-scaled GINE graph classifier and one-class encoders with rule risk for triage on Windows memory dumps27. Volatile RAM snapshots, however, retain live kernel structures—active process trees, memory protections, and cached volatile registry keys—that vanish once a system powers down30.

### **Where Premise 2 Holds—and the Near-Neighbors You Must Differentiate**

Your second premise—that dead-disk forensic tools treat artifacts as flat, isolated rows grouped by timestamps—is accurate for the **open-source triage stack** commonly paired with dissect. Plaso (log2timeline) flattens heterogeneous artifacts into chronological super-timelines without structural relationships32; Hayabusa applies Sigma rules to .evtx files to produce flat CSV/JSON timelines, leaving any Neo4j graph analysis to external post-processing of event logs34; KAPE and Eric Zimmerman's EZ Tools (MFTECmd, PECmd, RECmd, AmcacheParser, LECmd) deliberately output unscored per-artifact CSVs for manual analyst pivoting35; and Fox-IT's dissect emits typed flow.record outputs whose published scalable workflows serialize records into timestamped JSONL for Timesketch or Elastic37. Even Timesketch's built-in graph plugins focus on narrow log-derived slices (such as logins, service launches, and downloads)41, while Autopsy's Central Repository performs exact-match *cross-case* correlation on hashes, emails, and device IDs rather than intra-host structural inference43.  
Nevertheless, claiming that *no* dead-disk tool or DFIR study constructs non-temporal artifact graphs or performs dead-disk scoring overlooks seven close neighbors in commercial DFIR and academic literature that reviewers will expect you to contrast explicitly.

Adjacent forensic frameworks reinforce this same boundary. Belkasoft X's Connection Graph maps *human communication networks* (calls, SMS, chats, emails) rather than OS artifacts58. An MDPI study on **HVEA-SIFTING** (November 2026\) organizes Windows artifacts into a 4-tier, 10-layer static inter-artifact dependency graph validated across Windows XP, Vista, and 11, but applies that schema-level graph exclusively to decide which files to selectively preserve during acquisition rather than for post-hoc anomaly inference60. Meanwhile, single-artifact ML studies—including Alsulami & Mancoridis (2018) and Duby et al. (2022) on Prefetch4, DS4N6 (2021) on Scheduled Tasks5, and Hong et al. (2026) on tabular NTFS USN Journal time slots (achieving 0.86 ROC-AUC and 0.77 F1)62—do not perform cross-artifact graph propagation.  
**Verdict on novelty:** The gap is real, well-defined, and defensible. No surveyed work combines **(1) deterministic, timestamp-free static pointer resolution across heterogeneous cold-disk Windows OS artifacts** with **(2) hub-attenuated anomaly score propagation over those pointers** to catch stealth persistence, self-deleting tooling, and abused signed binaries that appear benign in isolation.

## **Why This Gap Matters Empirically**

Beyond filling an academic void, empirical evaluations published between 2020 and late 2026 demonstrate that both flat static persistence scanners and log-dependent provenance detectors fail systematically under realistic attacker tradecraft.  
![][image2]  
First, **static persistence detection remains far from solved**. A June 2026 ASIA CCS systematization of Windows malware persistence cataloged 72 distinct techniques spanning the Registry, File System, WMI databases, and hybrid Registry-plus-File-System mechanisms, observing that 55.2% of evaluated real-world malware samples establish persistence63. Benchmarked across all 72 techniques, industry-standard static tools exhibited substantial blind spots: **Autoruns** suffered a 24.9% False Negative Rate (FNR), **PersistenceSniper** suffered a 34.9% FNR (supporting only 38 of 72 techniques), and **Capa** (prior to updated rules) suffered a 42.1% FNR alongside a 72.5% False Positive Rate (FPR) driven by overly broad thread-scope matching63. Attackers routinely evade flat scanners through path obfuscation (mixed capitalization or trailing whitespace), DLL hijacking, or invoking persistence through less-monitored subsystems such as WMI63.  
Second, **both runtime audit logs and forensic timestamps degrade under realistic operational limits and active adversaries**. An October 2026 arXiv preprint auditing 38 provenance-era detector papers (arXiv:2610.35151) found that 28 of 38 systems trust log capture or storage—or place tampering out of scope—and none specifies which derived conclusions survive deleted, delayed, or forged records64. Even absent deliberate wiping, default Windows event-log buffers can roll over rapidly: an independent DFIR practitioner testing WMI persistence on Forensic Focus noted default size caps of just 1 MB for WMI-Activity/Operational, roughly 15 MB for PowerShell/Operational, and 64 MB for Sysmon66. Timestamp-based timeline grouping is equally fragile: Breitinger et al. (*FSI: Digital Investigation*, 2020\) evaluated \$MFT, \$LogFile, \$UsnJrnl, .lnk files, Prefetch, and Windows Event Logs against Timestomp, SetMACE, and nTimestomp, concluding that none of the analyzed NTFS timestamp artifacts can withstand active exploitation67. A stateless, timestamp-free referential graph is structurally invariant to timestomping and does not depend on EVTX retention—though it remains bounded by the survival of underlying structural artifacts such as \$MFT, Registry hives, Tasks, and Prefetch or Amcache, which an adversary with administrative privileges can still disable or purge4.  
Third, **self-deletion and Living-off-the-Land tradecraft defeat isolated per-artifact scoring**. Auditing MITRE ATT\&CK, Duby et al. (2022) found that 29.8% of threat actors and 33.7% of malware campaigns employ self-deletion, depriving examiners of the binary needed for AV or YARA inspection4. At the same time, Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBins) are legitimately Microsoft-signed OS executables whose static PE attributes and NSRL hash lookups look entirely clean47. Even strong tabular artifact prioritizers—such as the Autoencoder \+ Logarithmic Entropy pipeline that concentrates malicious artifacts into the top 2.6% of ranked output compared to DS4N6's 12.3% across 6,271 compromised systems5—evaluate each record independently. When a signed OS binary (rundll32.exe, mshta.exe, ie4uinit.exe) is triggered by an obfuscated Scheduled Task or loads an unexpected DLL or .inf payload73, the malicious signal exists strictly in the cross-artifact referential chain.

## **Engineering the Dead-Disk Referential Graph: Static Pointers and Silent Windows Traps**

Translating Concept A into a dissect-based system on cold Windows NTFS overlays requires treating OS artifacts as a **three-tier typed pointer network** rather than flat strings. Concretely, consider a stealth LOLBin and DLL-sideloading intrusion reconstructed without a single timestamp or event log. At the **Persistence Layer**, a suspiciously located Scheduled Task XML file (or a registry-only TaskCache entry) points either directly via command-line invocation to a signed hosting binary or indirectly via a \<ComHandler\> ClassId GUID to a Registry CLSID\\{GUID}\\InprocServer32 key74. At the **Execution Residue Layer**, that invocation maps to a context-scoped node for the signed binary (such as rundll32.exe) linked via a command-line-inclusive Prefetch hash match to its corresponding .pf record77. At the **NTFS MFT Layer**, the .pf record's File Metrics array exposes three distinct classes of static targets: heavily connected universal OS hubs (ntdll.dll, kernel32.dll) whose influence must be attenuated80, a rare DLL residing in a user-writable directory jointly referenced by both the Prefetch MFT file reference and the InprocServer32 target path, and—if the attacker used a self-deleting dropper—a deleted payload whose 8-byte MFT file reference triggers a sequence-number mismatch (a dangling reference)78.

### **The Static Referential Pointer Schema (Extractable via Dissect)**

To separate a true referential graph from brittle filename string matching, your extractor should prioritize **binary indices, cryptographic hashes, GUID indirections, and OS-resolved paths**. All major Windows sources below are accessible through dissect.target plugins (including mft, prefetch, registry/runkeys, tasks, amcache, usnjrnl, sru, and dissect.shellitem39), yet each carries silent Windows or NTFS resolution traps that will drop true attack edges or fabricate false links if ignored.

| Source Artifact | Static Pointer / Resolution Key | Resolved Target Node | Semantic Edge Type | Critical Windows / NTFS Engineering Trap |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Prefetch (.pf v23/v26/v30)**78 | File Metrics Array **8-byte NTFS File Reference** (6-byte MFT index \+ 2-byte seq) | \$MFT File / DLL Record | LOADED\_RESOURCE / ACCESSED\_FILE | MFT slot reuse increments the sequence number by 1 upon deletion; naive index-only joins create false edges81. |
| **Prefetch Filename / Header**77 | Executable name (max 29 chars) \+ 32-bit SCCA path hash | \$MFT Executable or Persistence Command Line | EXECUTED\_BINARY | Hosting apps (svchost, rundll32, dllhost, mmc) and /prefetch:\[0-8\] fold command-line arguments and \\DEVICE\\HARDDISKVOLUME\# into version-specific SCCA hashes77. |
| **Scheduled Tasks (XML \+ TaskCache)**49 | \<Exec\>\<Command\> \+ \<Arguments\>, or \<ComHandler\>\<ClassId\>{GUID} | \$MFT Binary, Script, or CLSID Registry Key | TRIGGERS\_EXEC / INVOKES\_COM | **GhostTask** writes directly to TaskCache Registry without creating an XML file on disk, or deletes the SD value to hide from Task Scheduler queries49. |
| **Registry CLSID / COM Keys**76 | InprocServer32 / LocalServer32 default value | \$MFT DLL / EXE Record | RESOLVES\_COM\_DLL | Requires modeling HKCU vs. HKLM precedence and Wow6432Node / SysWOW64 32-bit redirection90. |
| **Registry Services (SYSTEM)**93 | ImagePath (REG\_EXPAND\_SZ) and Parameters\\ServiceDll | \$MFT Service EXE or Hosted DLL | RUNS\_SERVICE / HOSTS\_SERVICEDLL | svchost.exe \-k \<Group\> services point their actual payload in Parameters\\ServiceDll rather than ImagePath93; paths require expanding environment variables such as %SystemRoot%91. |
| **Registry Run / ASEP Keys**63 | Value command string (Run, RunOnce, Winlogon, ASEPs) | \$MFT Binary \+ Parsed Arg Targets | PERSISTS\_AT\_LOGON | Path obfuscation (mixed case, trailing whitespace, 8.3 short names, quoted args, and NTFS ADS executables like notepad.exe:evil.exe)63. |
| **WMI Repository (OBJECTS.DATA)**66 | \_\_EventFilter → \_\_FilterToConsumerBinding → CommandLine/ActiveScriptEventConsumer | \$MFT Payload / scrcons.exe / Embedded Script | WMI\_SUBSCRIPTION\_EXEC | Resides in compressed binary CIM database (\\wbem\\Repository\\OBJECTS.DATA); fileless scripts live inline inside the consumer object rather than as standalone files98. |
| **LNK Shortcuts & ShellBags**100 | BEEF0004 extension block (MFT index, seq \#) \+ TrackerDataBlock \$OBJECT\_ID \+ Volume Serial | \$MFT File Record & USBSTOR / Volume Node | REFERENCES\_FILE / RESIDED\_ON\_VOLUME | Survives file moves/renames via \$OBJECT\_ID and bridges disconnected removable media to host registry keys via Volume Serial1. |
| **Amcache (Amcache.hve)**36 | InventoryApplicationFile FileId ("0000" \+ SHA-1) & LowerCaseLongPath | \$MFT PE File / ProgramId Cluster | INVENTORIED\_BINARY | Practitioner documentation notes FileId hashes only the **first 31 MiB** (not full files \>31 MiB), and the roughly daily Compatibility Appraiser misses short-lived intra-day drops36. |
| **NTFS \$MFT & \$I30 / \$UsnJrnl**81 | \$FILE\_NAME Parent (MFT index, seq \#), \$ATTRIBUTE\_LIST, ADS \$DATA | Parent Directory MFT Record | CONTAINS\_CHILD / ORPHAN\_OF | Reused parent directory slots silently attach deleted child files to unrelated folders unless parent sequence numbers are validated81. |

### **Turning OS Quirks Into Structural Signals**

Rather than burying these Windows intricacies in an appendix, formalizing four resolution mechanisms directly strengthens your systems contribution.  
**Forward Command-Line Prefetch Hashing for Hosting Applications.** Analysts ordinarily treat svchost.exe, rundll32.exe, dllhost.exe, and mmc.exe Prefetch hashes as opaque because Windows incorporates command-line arguments and /prefetch:\[0-8\] flags alongside the \\DEVICE\\HARDDISKVOLUME\# path into its 32-bit SCCA hash77. Because your graph already parses candidate command lines from Scheduled Tasks, Services, Run keys, LNK files, and WMI consumers, running the OS-version-specific SCCA hashing algorithm forward over extracted (device\_path, command\_line) pairs (iterating candidate HARDDISKVOLUME\# indices when volume mapping is ambiguous) lets you link a specific persistence configuration directly onto its exact hosting-app .pf file86. Two practical caveats must be documented honestly: libscca's public specification still marks Windows 10 v30 command-line hashing details as incomplete78 (requiring empirical verification on your target Windows 10/11 builds), and DFIR guidance emphasizes that a .pf file can be created even if a launch failed and supports execution *inference* rather than standalone proof70. Even with those caveats, Prefetch's DLL list is remarkably complete—Duby et al. (2022) observed that only 1.8% of evaluated executions had DLLs in process memory absent from their Prefetch file4.  
**Dangling and Sequence-Mismatched MFT References as First-Class Features.** When NTFS deletes a file, its MFT entry is marked free and its sequence number increments by 1 while retaining metadata until overwritten81. Validating any Prefetch File Metrics or LNK BEEF0004 reference (mft\_index, seq) against \$MFT therefore yields three unambiguous structural states: *live-matched* (in\_use and record.seq \== seq), *deleted-unreused* (\!in\_use and record.seq \- 1 \== seq), and *deleted-and-reused* (sequence mismatch beyond deletion increment)81. Because 33.7% of malware campaigns self-delete4—as seen in Cobalt Strike SMB Beacon attacks where a randomly named binary in C:\\Windows\\ is removed immediately after execution, leaving only its Service entry and .pf traces82—a persistence or execution node pointing to a dangling or sequence-mismatched MFT slot provides a high-signal, timestamp-free anomaly edge attribute.  
**Graceful Degradation on Prefetch-Disabled Windows Servers.** Prefetch is disabled by default on Windows Server (EnablePrefetcher \= 0), and on Windows 8/10/11 workstations it rolls over past 1,024 entries while monitoring only the first \~10 seconds of startup70. A design that collapses without .pf files will fail on Domain Controllers and enterprise servers. Your graph schema must therefore treat Prefetch as one execution-residue layer alongside **Amcache** (computing 31 MiB prefix SHA-1 digests on live MFT binaries to resolve FileId links36), **Shimcache (AppCompatCache)**, **SRUM (SRUDB.dat)**, **BAM/DAM**, **UserAssist**, and **LNK/JumpLists**97, and your evaluation should explicitly ablate workstation images (Prefetch enabled) against server images (Prefetch disabled).  
**Cross-Artifact Parity Edges for Stealth Tampering.** Structural disagreements across static stores can be encoded directly as typed contradiction edges rather than ad-hoc scripts: reconciling C:\\Windows\\System32\\Tasks XML files against SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\Schedule\\TaskCache surfaces GhostTask registry-only tasks and stripped Security Descriptors49; reconciling Prefetch against Amcache surfaces intra-appraiser drops executed and deleted between daily Compatibility Appraiser runs71; and diffing active hives against Volume Shadow Copies (when present) exposes deliberate hive cleanup71.

## **The Algorithmic Core: Solving Static Hub Collapse in Anomaly Propagation**

If pointer resolution is the systems foundation of Concept A, **hub-safe anomaly propagation** is its core algorithmic challenge—and the exact mechanism where a naive graph implementation breaks down.  
In runtime provenance research, a decade of work has targeted **dependency explosion**, where long-running processes or shared files link thousands of benign and malicious flows so that unchecked propagation taints the entire host graph9. MORSE (IEEE S\&P 2020\) mitigated this using asymmetric subject-tag modulation and exponential decay9, NoDoze (NDSS 2019\) paired behavioral execution partitioning with regularity-score network diffusion10, and DepImpact (USENIX Security 2022\) learned LDA-projected discriminative edge weights13.  
A Dead-Disk Referential Graph faces an equally severe static analogue: **Universal OS Hub Collapse**, driven by two ubiquitous node classes. First, **universal resource hubs** appear everywhere—Duby et al. (2022) found that core libraries such as ntdll.dll, kernel32.dll, and kernelbase.dll appear in *every* Windows Prefetch file80, while directories like C:\\Windows\\System32 anchor thousands of \$MFT entries. Second, **polymorphic execution supernodes**—signed OS utilities such as svchost.exe, powershell.exe, cmd.exe, rundll32.exe, conhost.exe, and dllhost.exe—legitimately connect to dozens of Scheduled Tasks, Services, and .pf records72. Running standard undirected Label Propagation, Belief Propagation, or a vanilla Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) over this raw topology triggers two simultaneous failure modes: **score smearing**, where suspicion from one malicious task leaks through powershell.exe or kernel32.dll onto unrelated benign binaries (the same hub-inflation distortion Liu et al. documented for popular web servers like google.com in unweighted HTTP score propagation25), and **over-smoothing**, where the overwhelming benign degree of svchost.exe or System32 washes out a weak anomaly arriving from one mislocated task or sideloaded DLL116.  
To overcome static hub collapse and outperform isolated tabular scoring, your propagation layer should incorporate four architectural design principles.  
**Context-Scoped Virtual Node Splitting.** Rather than merging every reference to rundll32.exe, svchost.exe, or powershell.exe into a single vertex, separate the **static on-disk PE file node** (holding Authenticode signature, hash, and \$MFT attributes) from **invocation-context nodes** (one per Scheduled Task action, Service configuration, WMI consumer, or command-line-hashed .pf record). Connect the static PE node to each context node via a *unidirectional* EXECUTES\_IMAGE edge that supplies baseline binary trust without allowing risk to traverse *back* across the shared binary into unrelated benign tasks. This accomplishes statically what execution partitioning accomplishes in runtime provenance graphs10.  
**Typed, Directional, IDF-Attenuated Edge Weights.** Adapting the TF-IDF edge-weighting intuition that proved effective in ARTISAN's Weighted Content Provenance Graph6, assign each Prefetch \--\[LOADED\_MODULE\]--\> File edge an Inverse Host Frequency (IHF) weight derived across all Prefetch files on the host (or across a benign enterprise baseline):  
![][image3]  
Under this formulation, universal OS libraries (ntdll.dll, kernel32.dll) referenced by nearly every Prefetch file automatically decay toward zero propagation weight, whereas a rare DLL residing in C:\\ProgramData\\ or C:\\Users\\Public\\ retains maximum coupling. Pair IDF attenuation with relation-specific directional transition weights: strong coupling along tight control-indirection edges (Task \-\> ComHandler \-\> InprocServer32 \-\> DLL, Service \-\> ServiceDll, Persistence \-\> PrefetchHashMatch) and heavily damped weights along loose containment edges (Directory \-\> File).  
**Scoring Referential Paths and Localized Subgraphs Rather Than Raw Files.** Revisit your motivating example of a valid signed binary triggered by a weirdly located Scheduled Task. Because C:\\Windows\\System32\\mshta.exe or ie4uinit.exe is genuinely a clean Microsoft binary, flagging the binary node itself creates analyst confusion. Borrowing from NoDoze's path anomaly scoring and MORSE's compact scenario graphs9, your output should rank **scored referential chains or compact ego-subgraphs** (for instance, (Anomalous Task) \-\> (Context: ie4uinit.exe) \-\> (Prefetch loading C:\\ProgramData\\ieuinit.inf)73). The underlying OS binary stays clean while the specific persistence-to-payload chain accumulates elevated joint risk.  
**Interpretable Propagation Head-to-Head Against Heterogeneous GNNs.** Do not jump straight to an opaque deep GNN without benchmarking interpretable propagation baselines such as typed Label Spreading, damped Belief Propagation over factor graphs119, or asymmetric score diffusion9. Forensically admissible triage requires tracing every elevated score back to explicit source artifacts and edge contributions55. Moreover, empirical evidence cautions against assuming deep GNNs automatically win: Bilot et al. (USENIX Security 2025\) showed that a simpler, well-engineered provenance detector (VELOX) outperformed complex deep GNN baselines on 8 of 9 benchmarks while avoiding severe cross-run instability7, and an arXiv preprint benchmarking threat-intelligence graph propagation in PySpark (arXiv:2411.06239) reported that Label Propagation ran over 5× faster than Loopy Belief Propagation with more predictable convergence while matching tuned Label Spreading26. Benchmarking both transparent typed diffusion/BP and a Heterogeneous GNN (such as R-GCN or Jumping-Knowledge GAT to mitigate over-smoothing121) lets you rigorously measure whether learned neural message passing adds genuine lift over auditable static propagation.

## **Evaluation Strategy and Publication Roadmap**

Recent meta-evaluations in 2025 and 2026 have sharply tightened empirical standards for both security graphs and forensic ML. Bilot et al. (USENIX Security 2025\) documented nine recurring pitfalls across PIDS papers—including post-threshold metric inflation via 2-hop neighborhood labeling (SC2), tuning hyperparameters on test data (SC4), failing to measure cross-run instability where Attack Detection Precision swings from 1.00 down to below 0.1 across identical runs (SC5), and fitting text embeddings on test sets (SC6)7. On the forensic side, Chudasama et al. (arXiv:2611.01225, October 2026\) formalized **label–signal mismatch** (showing an injection heuristic fired on 53% of supposedly "benign" rows in a cited 2021 corpus) and proved that matched-pair leave-one-family-out AUROC is three-valued and easily confounded when curation rules leak into learned graph attributes27. Avoiding these exact pitfalls from the outset will substantially strengthen your evaluation.

### **Constructing a Defensible Cold-Disk Evaluation Corpus**

Because real-world forensic disk images are rarely shareable due to privacy and legal constraints125, a credible evaluation should combine three complementary tiers of NTFS disk images rather than relying solely on clean lab VMs.  
First, build a **controlled ground-truth benchmark using ForTrace / ForTrace++** (Göbel et al., DFRWS EU 2022; agentless hypervisor conversion by Wolf et al., DFRWS EU 2024; Rzepka et al., 2025\)126. Because ForTrace++ drives QEMU/KVM guests via the hypervisor without a client-side simulation agent, it avoids contaminating disk images with test-harness remnants while synthesizing realistic multi-week background noise alongside scripted attacks126. Populate scenarios covering a diverse cross-section of the 72 Windows persistence classes systematized at ASIA CCS 202663, prioritizing the cases where isolated scanners fail: signed LOLBins launched via Scheduled Tasks, Services, and COM InprocServer32 hijacks; DLL sideloading; GhostTask TaskCache tampering; WMI OBJECTS.DATA subscriptions; and self-deleting payloads.  
Second, validate out-of-distribution performance on **public third-party NTFS disk images**. The **ADFIR (2025)** synthetic and CTF forensic corpus (Mendeley Data 65g9gm8zrd) pairs simulated APT post-exploitation traces with full E01 disk images from *The Stolen Szechuan Sauce*—including both a Windows Server 2012 R2 Domain Controller (DC01, with 111,850 \$MFT records and 82,085 \$J records, ideal for testing Prefetch-disabled server degradation) and a Windows 10 Desktop workstation containing coreupdater.exe relocated to C:\\Windows\\System32 with Service and Run-key persistence—alongside Magnet CTF 2019/2022 and NIST CFReDS Data Leakage and Hacking Case images97. Note that the ADFIR documentation snippet does not expose unified machine-readable ground-truth labels across all scenarios97, so ground-truth validation on CTF images must be explicitly documented and separated from synthetic training data.  
Third, stress-test false positive rates against **"dirty" benign controls**. Enterprise Windows hosts routinely run software updaters (TiWorker.exe, Office Click-to-Run), third-party svchost-hosted services, and legitimate maintenance scripts stored in C:\\ProgramData or C:\\Windows\\Temp106. Including aged, software-heavy benign workstations—and auditing them for label–signal mismatch28—ensures your detector does not overfit to sterile OS installs.

### **Mandatory Baselines, Ablations, and Metrics Checklist**

To prove that **propagating risk across static dead-disk pointers** delivers the detection lift—rather than feature engineering alone—structure your experiments around five concrete comparisons:

> 1. **Static Persistence Scanners:** Benchmark recall and precision against offline **Autoruns** and **PersistenceSniper**63 on COM hijacks, GhostTask, DLL sideloading, and LOLBin Scheduled Tasks.  
> 2. **Tabular Per-Artifact ML Baselines (No Graph):** Implement the **Autoencoder \+ Logarithmic Entropy** prioritizer5 and Duby et al.'s **Prefetch-only Jaccard kNN**4 on the exact same dissect-extracted artifact features to isolate the incremental gain from graph structure.  
> 3. **Timestamp-Windowed and Log-Dependent Baseline Under Anti-Forensics:** Group the identical artifacts by temporal proximity windows (mirroring Plaso/GATOR-style co-occurrence53) and evaluate both *before* and *after* adversarial timestomping (SetMACE/Timestomp) and EVTX clearing67. Demonstrating stable detection while temporal/log baselines collapse delivers your sharpest empirical contrast.  
> 4. **Propagation & Hub-Mitigation Ablations:** Compare (a) unpropagated local node scores, (b) naive undirected propagation without hub attenuation (empirically quantifying static hub collapse), (c) context-split \+ IDF-attenuated interpretable propagation (typed diffusion / Label Spreading / factor-graph BP), and (d) Heterogeneous GNNs (R-GCN / Jumping-Knowledge GAT).  
> 5. **Triage Utility, Stability, and Traceability Reporting:** Report **top-k triage concentration** (percentage of ranked subgraphs or artifacts inspected to uncover 100% of malicious chains, directly comparable to the 2.6% vs. 12.3% benchmark5), **Attack Detection Precision (ADP)** without 2-hop neighborhood inflation7, **multi-seed variance** across ≥5 runs7, strict separation between rule-derived features and learned representations with zero test-set embedding leakage7, and **evidentiary traceability** distinguishing source-grounded pointer assertions (MFT record IDs, registry paths, byte offsets) from computed propagation paths55.

### **Recommended Venue Positioning**

Two publication tracks fit Concept A naturally, depending on where you concentrate depth. **DFRWS (USA / EU) and *Forensic Science International: Digital Investigation*** offer the highest natural alignment if your centerpiece is the dissect-based cold NTFS architecture, deep binary pointer resolution (Prefetch v30 File Metrics, forward SCCA command-line hashing, BEEF0004, MFT sequence validation, TaskCache-vs-XML parity, and Amcache 31 MiB prefix matching), evidentiary traceability, and an open-source release—directly advancing the trajectory set by FEAR (DFDS 2025), HVEA-SIFTING (2026), and GATOR (DFRWS USA 2026\)3. **USENIX Security, NDSS, ACSAC, or ASIA CCS** become strong targets if you emphasize the adversarial logless and timestomp-resilient threat model (contrasting directly with ARTISAN at USENIX Security 2024 and the 28 of 38 log-trusting PIDS detectors audited in arXiv:2610.351516), formalize static hub collapse and context-scoped propagation mathematically, and benchmark broadly against the persistence evasion classes cataloged at ASIA CCS 202663.  
In either venue, position the paper not as "nobody has ever graphed dead disks," but as **the first stateless, timestamp-free, pointer-resolved dead-disk inference engine that solves static OS hub collapse to outperform both isolated tabular artifact scoring and log-dependent provenance graphs on stealth persistence, self-deleting payloads, and abused signed binaries.**
